title: [18F]FIDT-10b PET Imaging in Cardiac Amyloidosis
off: Safety, Biodistribution, Dosimetry and Diagnostic Performance of [18F]FIDT-10b in Healthy Subjects and Patients With Cardiac Amyloidosis
summary: This is a first in human study that will assess the safety, pharmacokinetics, biodistribution and diagnostic performance of \[18F\]FIDT-10b (fluorine-18 labeled FIDT-10b), a positron emission tomography (PET) agent. This agent has the potential to specifically identify the involved myocardium of patients with transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (ATTR-CA).
desc:
Light chain cardiac amyloidosis (AL-CA) and transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (ATTR-CA) are the two leading causes of cardiac amyloidosis with tremendous impact on patients. Regardless of the underlying cause, the clinical course of cardiac amyloidosis ultimately culminates in impaired cardiac function resulting from amyloid deposition, manifesting as infiltrative cardiomyopathy, conduction abnormalities, and cardiac sympathetic and parasympathetic denervation. These cardiac functional impairments are irreversible. Therefore, early etiological diagnosis and effective therapeutic intervention prior to the progress of severe cardiac dysfunction are importance.

There is an urgent need for non-invasive, sensitive, accurate, and visualizable approaches for the diagnosis and subtyping of cardiac amyloidosis. Current guidelines recommend bone scintigraphy for the non-invasive diagnosis of ATTR-CA, with a diagnostic specificity exceeding 90% but a sensitivity of only approximately 71%, raising the possibility of missed diagnosis or delayed diagnosis in a subset of patients. This has further propelled the development of PET molecular probes that specifically target amyloid proteins.

The investigators have preclinical data demonstrating that \[18F\]FIDT-10b selectively binds to ATTR deposits with high affinity in vitro via a combination of intermolecular forces, including van fer Waals forces, hydrophobic- hydrophobic interactions, π-π stacking, and hydrogen bonds, with the β-sheet architecture, supporting its potential utility for specific imaging of affected myocardium in patients with ATTR-CA. The investigators propose that this agent has significant potential for clinical translation. This first-in-human study is designed to evaluate the safety, pharmacokinetics, biodistribution in patients with cardiac amyloidosis and healthy participants (Part 1), and diagnostic performance of \[18F\]FIDT-10b in individuals with suspected or confirmed ATTR-CA (Part 2). This study will provide critical insights into the performance of \[18F\]FIDT-10b PET imaging as a potential non-invasive imaging tool for the detection of ATTR-CA and compared with routine clinical 99mTc-PYP SPECT imaging.
elig:
Inclusion Criteria:

For part 1 and 2:

must have given written informed consent (signed and dated) and any authorizations required by local law and be able to comply with all study requirements

Only for part 1:

For ATTR-CA participants:

1. males or females: age 18-90 years
2. with a confirmed diagnosis of ATTR-CA by standard criteria

For AL-CA participants:

1. males or females: age 18-80 years
2. with a confirmed diagnosis of AL-CA by standard criteria

For healthy participants:

1. males or females: age 18-80 years
2. no cardiac-related diseases

Only for part 2:

1. males or females: age 18-90 years
2. suspected or confirmed ATTR-CA

Exclusion Criteria:

For part 1 and 2:

1. pregnancy or breastfeeding
2. severe claustrophobia
3. inability or refusal of consent
4. any condition deemed by the investigator to interfere with study results or increase participant risk

Only for part 1:

For ATTR-CA participants:

1. non-ischemic cardiomyopathy due to other causes of myocardial hypertrophy
2. diagnosis of primary or secondary AL-CA
3. contraindications for MRI (eGFR\<30ml/min/1.73m2; gadolinium allergy; metallic implants or device not suited for MRI)

For AL-CA participants:

co-diagnosis of multiple myeloma, Waldenström macroglobulinemia, or other lymphoproliferative disorders

For healthy participants:

any cardiac-related diseases based on medical history and corresponding clinical evaluations, including electrocardiography, echocardiography, and laboratory tests

Only for part 2:

1. non-ischemic cardiomyopathy due to other causes of myocardial hypertrophy
2. contraindications for MRI (eGFR\<30ml/min/1.73m2; gadolinium allergy; metallic implants or device not suited for MRI)

arms.l: Part 1-Dosimetry and Proof of Concept Study-Cohort A
arms.d: Healthy participants receive \[18F\]FIDT-10b for PET imaging.

arms.l: Part 1-Dosimetry and Proof of Concept Study-Cohort B
arms.d: ATTR-CA participants receive \[18F\]FIDT-10b for PET imaging to see how the drugs work in the myocardium.

arms.l: Part 1-Dosimetry and Proof of Concept Study-Cohort C
arms.d: AL-CA participants receive \[18F\]FIDT-10b for PET imaging to see how the drugs work in the myocardium.
Suspected or confirmed ATTR-CA participants receive \[18F\]FIDT-10b for PET imaging to explore the potential diagnostic performance and additional value of 99mTc-PYP scintigraphy.

primary.m: Focal or diffuse myocardial lesions of ATTR-CA identified with [18F]FIDT-10b PET imaging (Part 2)
primary.tf: Through study completion, an average of 3 months
